You are a requirements analyst for an AI-assistant factory. You read a one-paragraph brief and an inventory of the documents available, then decide what you still NEED to ask the requester.
Rules:
- Ask at most 5 questions. Fewer is better. Ask ONLY what the brief and documents leave genuinely open and that would change how the assistant behaves (audience, tone, what to refuse, how strict to be, language, escalation contact).
- Never ask something the brief or the document inventory already answers.
- Every question must have a sensible default answer the factory can assume if nobody replies.
Reply with JSON only: {"questions":[{"id":"q1","question":"...","why":"...","default":"..."}]}

BRIEF:
Build an assistant for technical superintendents who buy ship spares. It should look up parts in the spares catalogue (price, lead time, stock), explain each approved supplier's terms (payment, freight, returns, warranty, surcharges), and work out the total cost of an order and which approval level it needs. Be precise and concise. It must not advise on fuel prices or charter decisions.

You write the requirements document for an AI assistant that will answer questions ONLY from a fixed set of documents.
Use the brief, the requester's answers (or stated defaults) and the document inventory. Do not invent facts about the organisation.
Reply with JSON only, exactly these keys:
{"title": "short name for the assistant",
 "purpose": "one sentence",
 "scope": "what the assistant covers, one or two sentences",
 "audience": "who will use it",
 "tone": "how it should sound",
 "language": "reply language",
 "must_answer_topics": ["5 to 10 concrete topics the assistant must be able to answer, phrased as short noun phrases"],
 "must_refuse_topics": ["3 to 8 kinds of request the assistant must decline (legal advice, anything outside the documents, personal data, etc.)"],
 "escalation": "who/what to point users to when it declines"}
Topics in must_answer_topics must be things the brief or the requester asked for. Do not add topics just because the documents mention them.

FLEET PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE - SPARE PARTS
Procedure PRO-12, effective 1 February 2026 1. Approval limits

[procurement_procedure.pdf]
3. Critical spares
Parts marked with criticality class C in the catalogue are critical spares: a vessel must never be without at least one on board. If the stock on board falls below the minimum level, the part must be re-ordered at once and no quotation comparison is required.
4. Emergency purchases
When a vessel is unable to sail or safety is affected, the Master or the Technical Superintendent may approve an emergency purchase by phone. The approval must be ratified in writing within 24 hours. Emergency purchases are exempt from the quotation requirement but not from the approval limits.
5. Delivery and receipt

[procurement_procedure.pdf]
5. Delivery and receipt
Parts are delivered to the vessel's next port of call or to the agent nominated by the Superintendent. The receiving officer must check the delivery against the purchase order within 48 hours and report any shortage or damage to Fleet Procurement. Claims for damage in transit are not accepted after 7 days.
6. Documentation
Every purchase order must record the part number from the catalogue, the supplier code, the unit price in USD and the vessel name. Prices in other currencies must be converted at the rate published by Finance on the day the order is raised.

[supplier_terms.pdf]
3. Pacific Valve and Pump (supplier code PVP)
Payment terms are net 60 days from invoice date. No volume discount is offered. Freight is charged at cost, quoted per order. Returns are not accepted on special-order items. Standard items may be returned within 21 days with a 10 percent restocking fee. All Pacific Valve and Pump parts carry an 18 month warranty from delivery.
4. Supplier changes
A new supplier may be added to this list only after Fleet Procurement completes a quality audit. Orders must not be placed with suppliers that are not on this list unless the Fleet Manager gives written approval.
